markers.name: Sub-floor fines size distribution
markers.proposition: Resolves the excess fine high-Z population of M2060 below the current detection floor, where it is now cut off by the pixel size.
markers.scientific_definition: Number-size distribution of high-Z (BSE-bright) objects per unit area, extended below the current detection floor and compared with approved micrographs imaged at the same pixel size.
markers.measurement_definition: Equivalent-diameter histogram of high-Z objects from BSE at a finer pixel (low kV), same segmentation rule as the engine; densities per 1000 µm² in bins below and above the current floor; approved micrographs imaged at the same settings.
markers.why_relevant: The REJECT rests on M2060, and its excess objects pile up at the detection floor: the decision-driving population is only partly observed.
markers.capture_requirements: Higher-magnification, low-kV BSE on M2060 and on approved micrographs. No new instrument capability: the same acquisition as the controller's ZOOM action.
markers.observable: The number and size distribution of fine high-Z objects below the present detection floor.
markers.scientific_question: Is M2060's excess a true fine-particle population or an artefact of scale truncation?

rules: a state is a function of categorical gates; a gate is a function of structured evidence; research prose never sets either
evidence from fixture bundles is displayed but never advances a gate, a demand or a state-driving count

scientific relevance / literature convergence: met = one strong source (STRONG DIRECT or STRONG TRANSFERABLE) and two independent supporting sources, uncontested; contested = a contradictory source at least as strong as the best support
a counted project record that fails a proposition contests scientific relevance; a failed robustness record makes a marker CONFOUNDED
a blindspot link is a relationship, not evidence: alone it leaves a marker CANDIDATE
a marker that measures a dimension the field records as not acquired is non-redundant by construction
capability demand counts only active, non-fixture marker cases; a credible demand has scientific relevance met
ADMITTED and RECOMMENDED additionally require a non-fixture review; a review cannot lift a case whose gates are not met
contradictory evidence is listed with the case it bears on and is never dropped

status_basis.ADMITTED: every evidence gate met (relevance, measurability, robustness, blindspot value, non-redundancy) and a recorded admission review
status_basis.TRACKABLE: scientific relevance and measurability with current capture are both met
status_basis.SUPPORTED: scientific relevance met (replicated, uncontested literature); measurability not yet met
status_basis.BUILDING: some evidence gate is partly supported; scientific relevance not met
status_basis.CANDIDATE: proposed; no evidence gate supported yet (links to blindspots are relationships, not evidence)
status_basis.UNAVAILABLE: current capture cannot observe it; it counts as demand on the capability it names
status_basis.CONFOUNDED: a tested confound explains the signal under current capture
status_basis.REJECTED: tested without decision value, fully redundant, or rejected by a recorded review
status_basis.INTEGRATED: the capability is part of the workflow (recorded review)
status_basis.RECOMMENDED: critical mass and an accepted integration case with a recorded review
status_basis.CRITICAL_MASS: convergent credible marker demand, uncontested literature convergence, a consequential blindspot and no adequate substitute
status_basis.BUILDING_CASE: multiple credible marker needs, or one need that closes a consequential blindspot
status_basis.WATCHING: one or weak marker need and no consequential blindspot
